what: The lane was given b1, b2, b3 and d, then (mid-task) dynamic sealing of workspace crates, then one front end a checkout (F1) as first priority, then memory at Relax's level as an equal target. Built and measured: the census and the first half of b1 (library rows at HIGH). Written, not built: the sealed definition with seal groups in the engine, and F1's list of what lower_writes makes a plan. b1's second half, b2, b3, d, F1 and dynamic sealing are not built.
cost: the report says not built for most of the brief
cause: each of F1, seal groups and F2 is a change across blaze-lower, the engine or the serve path with its own simulation; reading the code to the point of a correct first change took most of the session
fix: three lanes with one outcome each: F1 (blaze-lower and unkept), seal groups (blaze-query row, function, storage), F2 with records read in place (hir-def deps and nameres::frozen)
whys: the brief grew by three outcomes while the first was being measured
each outcome meets a different 1,500 to 3,000 line file that had to be read first
nothing sized the steps against a session before they were handed over
class: a brief larger than one context can read the code for
prevention: a brief names one outcome whose files total a size one agent can read (rule every-agent-has-a-task); additions mid-task go to a new lane unless they are the same files
